patch_description: The weakest metrics are noise_reduction (0.33), false_reversals (21.4), and slope_changes (24.6). The champion cascade already achieves near-zero lag and perfect efficiency, so the safe way to attack the remaining noise gap is a *final zero-phase polishing stage*: a small odd-length (7-tap) quadratic Savitzky-Golay pass applied to the Stage-5 output. Because SG is a symmetric, zero-phase FIR smoother, it adds **no group delay** — lag_error and responsiveness stay intact — while it further suppresses the residual high-frequency noise that survives the hysteresis snap. Its short window (7) preserves genuine trend dynamics and cannot introduce the endpoint/length contract issues that killed over-elaborate generations. Following the common-thread guidance, the new stage ships with the same defensive clamps as the champion's sg_win handling (odd-length clamp, min 5, bounded by signal length), is purely additive at the end of the cascade (no slope-domain rewriting, no parameter mutation of existing stages), and keeps the length contract and O(n) cost (savgol is a fixed-tap convolution).
